title: Elodie and the Choir
premise: Mirabel Iversen, the youngest and last apprentice of the Ledgerkeepers—a guild that trades in impossible things—discovers tonight's date inscribed in a prophecy book written a century ago. When a stranger named Elodie arrives claiming to be the voice of a choir that once bound kings, Mirabel learns the prophecy names him: the one who must unbind King Aldric from the thing wearing his crown before the moon completes its thirteenth turn. Hunted by crown agents and betrayed by his own guildmaster, who sold the guild's secrets to survive, Mirabel and Elodie gather the scattered remnants of the choir—outcasts who each carry one note of the binding song. In the final confrontation beneath the thirteenth moon, Mirabel realizes the ledger was never a record but an instrument: he must sing his own name into it, erasing himself from history to free the king. The choir refuses to let him vanish alone, rewriting the entry together so that instead of one name erased, a new guild is written into being—with Mirabel, no longer the last of anything, at its heart.
about_author: E. M. Voss is the pen name of a former church chorister turned archivist who spent a decade cataloguing obscure trade ledgers in northern port cities. Their fiction blends bureaucratic magic with quiet stories of people finding the families they were never given.

chapters.title: The Weight of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. In the crumbling Ledgerkeeper's hall, Mirabel catalogs impossible trades—a bottled echo, a debt paid in years—while the guild's last members dwindle to three. His guildmaster, Corvane, dismisses his questions about a locked prophecy book. Emotional beat: lonely competence, the ache of being the last apprentice of a dying craft.

chapters.title: Tonight's Date, Written Long Ago
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The locked prophecy book falls open on its own, and Mirabel finds tonight's date inked a century past, followed by his own name. Terrified, he confronts Corvane, who goes pale and orders him to burn it. Emotional beat: dread curdling into defiance—the first time Mirabel disobeys.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Knocked Twice
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A stranger arrives at the guild door as the prophecy foretold, humming a chord that makes the candles lean. Elodie claims to be the last voice of the Choir of Binding, which once caged something inside King Aldric's crown—and the cage is failing. Emotional beat: wary recognition between two people who are each the last of something.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Through a scrying entry in the ledgers, Mirabel witnesses the court: King Aldric moving like a puppet, his eyes flickering with something ancient and hungry. The thing in the crown is waking faster because someone at court is feeding it. Emotional beat: horror tempered by pity for the trapped king.

chapters.title: Corvane's Bargain
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie discovers Corvane has been trading ledger secrets to the crown's spymaster in exchange for sparing the guild—betraying every impossible thing they protect. She warns Mirabel, who refuses to believe her. Emotional beat: the sting of truth delivered too plainly, and denial as self-protection.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Deciphering the prophecy's arithmetic, Mirabel calculates the deadline: thirteen lunar turns until the binding fails completely. They have barely half that. He commits to the quest, formally taking custody of the guild's ledgers—the first act of leadership he's ever claimed. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The First Note
chapters.summary: Dual POV. In a flooded quarry town, they find Sable, a disgraced opera singer whose voice can crack stone—one note of the choir. She agrees only after hearing Mirabel read aloud her own erased history from the ledgers, restoring what was taken from her. Emotional beat: the healing power of being remembered.

chapters.title: Crown Agents at the Door
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Crown agents raid the quarry town hunting 'the ledger boy.' The three flee through the flooded tunnels, and Sable uses her voice to collapse a passage behind them—revealing she's run from the crown before. Emotional beat: found family forming under fire, trust earned in escape.

chapters.title: A Debt Paid in Years
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. To cross the border ward, Mirabel must honor an old guild contract: a farmer once paid the guild thirty years of his life, and Mirabel must return them—which ages the man back to vigor but costs Mirabel a month of his own memories. Emotional beat: learning that the guild's magic always demands payment, and choosing to pay anyway.

chapters.title: The Second Note
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. In a mountain monastery they find Brother Oren, a mute monk who sings through vibration alone—the second note. He reveals Elodie's secret: she isn't merely the choir's last voice; she is its composed remnant, made from the choir itself when it was broken. Emotional beat: Elodie confronting that she may be more instrument than person.

chapters.title: Am I a Person or a Song?
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Shaken by Oren's revelation, Elodie confesses to Mirabel that she doesn't remember a childhood because she never had one. Mirabel shows her a blank page in the ledger and tells her unwritten things can still be written. Emotional beat: vulnerability met with acceptance—the heart of their bond.

chapters.title: The Court of Hollow Eyes
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Disguised as tax assessors, they infiltrate the capital and witness the courtiers' glassy obedience. Mirabel finds the spymaster's office and discovers Corvane's correspondence—and worse, evidence the spymaster serves the thing in the crown directly. Emotional beat: cold fury at betrayal, sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Corvane's Confession
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Cornered by Mirabel in the guild hall, Corvane breaks: he sold the guild not for gold but because the thing in the crown promised to restore the guild's dead—including Mirabel's parents, killed in a purge decades ago. Emotional beat: grief revealed as the root of treachery; Mirabel's anger softening into sorrow.

chapters.title: The Third Note
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The third note is held by a child, Wren, a street thief whose whistle can still the wind—an orphan like the choir itself. Convincing her means beating her at her own game: Sable trades her most precious memory for Wren's trust. Emotional beat: sacrifice freely given, family chosen over blood.

chapters.title: The Spymaster's Net
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Ambushed en route to the old choir chapel, the group is captured. In the cells, the spymaster offers Mirabel his parents' restoration if he surrenders the ledgers. Mirabel, tempted, looks at Elodie, Sable, Oren, and Wren—and refuses. Emotional beat: the false family of the past rejected for the true family of the present.

chapters.title: Escape Written in Ink
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren picks their locks while Mirabel writes an escape into the ledger itself—bribing reality with a trade: the prison's silence for their freedom. They flee to the ruined chapel where the choir was first bound. Emotional beat: ingenuity and audacity; the ledger becomes a weapon of hope rather than record.

chapters.title: The Broken Choir's History
chapters.summary: Oren's POV. In the chapel murals, the full truth emerges: the choir didn't imprison a demon—it imprisoned a dying god-king's hunger to live forever, and the original king begged for the binding. Aldric's ancestor stole the crown and the binding twisted. Emotional beat: moral complexity; the enemy is hunger, not evil, and mercy may be the answer.

chapters.title: Rehearsal Under a Waning Moon
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. With four notes gathered and two turns left, the group rehearses the unbinding song—but it requires five voices, and the fifth part is written for 'the keeper of the book.' Mirabel realizes the prophecy meant him all along. Emotional beat: terror of destiny accepted, transformed by the choir's faith in him.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Turn Falls
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The thing in the crown, desperate, unleashes its court upon the chapel. Corvane arrives—not to fight, but to stand with Mirabel, buying time with the guild's last stored miracle and falling in the defense. Emotional beat: costly redemption; forgiveness extended too late but given fully.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Moon
chapters.summary: Full-cast climax. Beneath the thirteenth moon, the choir sings the unbinding as the crown-thing tears free of Aldric. The final verse demands a name surrendered to the ledger—and Mirabel begins singing his own. But the choir joins him, writing all their names together, so the price is shared and the entry transforms: not an erasure but a founding. The hunger, offered belonging instead of a cage, dissolves. Aldric wakes, freed. Emotional beat: triumph through shared sacrifice; identity rewritten collectively.

chapters.title: A New Guild, Written In
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Weeks later, the Ledgerkeepers' hall reopens with new members drawn by rumor of the miracle. Elodie, now able to write her own history, signs the first page. Mirabel enters the guild's new charter: no longer trading in impossible things, but making them possible—together. Emotional beat: quiet joy; belonging achieved, not found.

chapters.title: The Next Blank Page
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. An epilogue: a new prophecy book stirs on the shelf, and fresh ink begins to bloom across a blank page bearing tomorrow's date. Elodie and Mirabel exchange a look—not fear this time, but readiness. Whatever comes, they will face it as a choir. Emotional beat: hopeful forward motion; the story ends as a beginning.
